summary: 8-byte-aligned allocation for a generic object allocator. Reads the allocator base from this+0x4, rejects requests over 0x3B9AC9F0 (error code 3), rounds the size up to the next 8-byte boundary, and for category a2 >= 2 writes a marker (constant 12 at obj+0x14, category at obj+0x18) and dispatches through the object vtable (obj+0, read as *a1). Allocates size+16 bytes through MallocWrapper (error code 4 on failure), accumulates the size into the running total at this+0x4C, then links the block into the per-category free list whose head lives at this+0x4 + 4*a2 + 56. Returns the payload pointer (block + 16 bytes).

local_names.a1: allocator object; a1[0] is the vtable pointer, a1[1] is the base used for free-list slots
local_names.a2: category index selecting the free-list slot
local_names.obj: sub-object reached through *a1, receiving the marker writes and vtable dispatch

operations.description: Cache the base pointer from this+0x4 (a1[1]) into v3 and copy the request size a3 into v4
Oversized request (a3 > 0x3B9AC9F0) invokes the error handler ShortComputation_5f0e with code 3
When (a3 & 7) != 0, round the size up to the next 8-byte boundary: v4 = a3 + 8 - (a3 & 7)
For category a2 >= 2: write constant 12 to obj+0x14 and category a2 to obj+0x18, then call the object vtable entry at obj+0 (dispatched through the pointer read at this+0x0)
Allocate v4+16 bytes via MallocWrapper; a null result invokes ShortComputation_5f0e with code 4
Accumulate the allocation size (v4+16) into the running total at this+0x4C, which is reached as this+0x4 + 72

Link the new block into the per-category free list: head slot at this+0x4 + 4*a2 + 56; block[0] = previous head, block[1] = v4, block[2] = 0; head slot updated to the block; payload returned at block + 4 (16 bytes)
Return the payload pointer (block header plus 16 bytes); called by MemoryAllocatorWithChunking (005160ad) and ChunkedBufferAlloc (0051613f)

unresolved: The marker writes (constant 12 and category index) only occur when a2 >= 2, and the vtable dispatch target is resolved at runtime so its behavior is unknown
Whether this allocator can split or reuse a previously freed block is not determinable; the observed behavior always allocates fresh via MallocWrapper
